_why: Every executable tracked in this repo is declared here with the bytes it is
supposed to have. scripts/verify_binaries.py enforces it, so an undeclared
binary or a changed one fails the build instead of riding along unread.
To add a binary: record its upstream URL and version, verify the download
yourself once (compare against the vendor's published hash where one exists,
or against a freshly downloaded copy), then paste the sha256 and size here.
'signature' records what scripts/verify_binaries.py observes today — a
downgrade from that state fails the build.

binaries.note: REPACKED, NOT PRISTINE. Arrived vendored inside the defender-remover toolkit rather than from Sordum directly. Its certificate directory is not a well-formed WIN_CERTIFICATE (declared length 776284822, revision 0xc496, type 14951 against the required 0x200/2) and 512 bytes trail it, so the Authenticode signature cannot validate. Its hash matches no Sordum release: official v1.6.0.0 x64 is da77bc401ef0d7b8e23be3a9387660172aea176cd9d1248034130811d29942c9 (934464 bytes) and current v1.9.0.0 x64 is b305126c2881073a53073bd1782d0649764d198562e02fc02395fc07637dcec5. Not known to be malicious — repacking is normal for that toolkit — but it is unverifiable. Replacing it with an official Sordum download would let this entry move to signature=valid.
